A participant experiment with saved code, predictions, and research-agent traces.
Anish Shah
Last updated: November 13, 2026
What I tested
In this CPU rehearsal, we built and tracked two forecasting experiments, then let a fixed research agent edit the image model code. The strongest first-round change zero-initialized the residual output head: validation error fell from 0.122116 to 0.111434. Round two tested masked L1 loss on that parent against an unchanged KEEP candidate; the selected L1 composition reached 0.110916. Each selected source was reviewed and tested before adoption.

On the reserved February 13–14 image dates, disk-masked absolute error was 0.125762 for persistence, 0.122442 for the manually implemented model, and 0.110011 for the adopted agent model (199 forecast windows). Inspect the saved first prediction at 2014-02-13 02:48 UTC and its disk-error image alongside the exact zero-init/L1 source. The two improvement rounds retained my manual harness, so there were two unique executable harnesses, not three. This run shows a working propose–probe–compose loop; it does not show a quality gain. The learner-written invoice tool ran in the manual two-invoices case with inv-1 and inv-2 and avoided a false duplicate refund. Onboarding traces show a committed write timing out, followed by a state read instead of another write. Eleven of twelve final explanation judgments are available and pass. One hit its output limit on both the original attempt and one explicit judge-only retry; its score remains missing, not zero, and the retry did not rerun the employee.
